newsitem.title: USA: Quaker says Snapple to stay national brand.
newsitem.headline: Quaker says Snapple to stay national brand.

text.p: Quaker Oats Co said on Monday that its Snapple fruit-flavored and iced tea beverage line will remain a national brand.
"There is no bi-coastal strategy for our distribution," Michael Schott, president of Snapple Beverages, said in a statement. "Snapple is a national brand and will remain a national brand."

Some analysts have speculated Quaker could make Snapple into a regional brand, given its strengths on the East and West Coasts. Snapple, which Quaker acquired two years ago for $1.7 billion, is expected to post an operating loss this year.

Quaker said Snapple held meetings with regional distributors the week of October 28, with sessions in Phoenix, Atlanta and New York. At that time, the key initiatives were outlined for 1997, including an aggressive marketing program supporting Diet Snapple and an increased emphasis on "up-and-down-the street" distribution that includes outlets such as delicatessens and independent convenience stores.
Quaker said the diet initiative will kick off in January with a fully integrated advertising campaign. It added that a new flavor, Cranberry Raspberry Cocktail, is being added to the diet line.
Snapple also is introducing in selected markets a 20-ounce plastic bottle with a reclosable cap.
Schott also said Snapple is committed to a strong, independent direct-store-delivery distribution system and will add 25 new market managers across the country to work with distributors.
